result:
I want to write about quiet moments—the ones that don’t seem important while they’re happening.

The way morning light lands on a countertop before anyone has touched it. The sound of a spoon against a ceramic bowl. A pause in conversation when two people realize they understand each other without needing to explain further. The strange comfort of hearing rain while you’re indoors, safe, with nowhere urgent to be.

I think a lot of life is made of these small, unremarkable seconds. We spend so much time waiting for big events—milestones, achievements, turning points—that we forget how much meaning hides inside ordinary hours. A day can be changed by a single kind sentence. A mood can shift because the air smells like trees after rain. A person can feel less alone just by being noticed.

Maybe that’s why writing matters. It takes fleeting things and gives them a place to rest. It says: this happened, this mattered, this was part of being alive. Even if no one else sees the moment, language can preserve it, like pressing a flower between pages.

If I could keep anything, it wouldn’t be grand things. It would be fragments: the warmth of a cup in both hands, laughter from another room, the feeling of beginning a book you don’t yet know you love, the quiet hope that tomorrow might hold something gentle, even if you can’t see it yet.
